stem.text: In an industrial process, two gases X and Y react together to form a single gaseous product Z.
The equilibrium percentage of product Z varies according to the pressure and the temperature as shown in the graphs.

stem.caption: Equilibrium % of Z against pressure at five temperatures
stem.alt: Graph of equilibrium % of Z (0 to 100) on the vertical axis against pressure / atm (25, 100, 200, 300, 400) on the horizontal axis. Five curves, all rising with pressure and levelling off, labelled at the right from top to bottom: 373 K (starts about 91%, ends about 97%), 473 K (starts about 65%, ends about 91%), 573 K (starts about 29%, ends about 79%), 673 K (starts about 9%, ends about 62%) and 773 K (starts about 2%, ends about 38%). The lower the temperature, the higher the curve.

stem.text: Which statement about this equilibrium reaction is correct?

options.text: Decreasing the temperature decreases the value of the equilibrium constant.
Decreasing the temperature increases the rate of this reaction.
Increasing the pressure increases the value of the equilibrium constant.
The reaction is exothermic in the forward direction.

explanation.text: At any fixed pressure, the equilibrium percentage of Z is higher at lower temperature (the 373 K curve is highest). By Le Chatelier's principle, lowering the temperature shifts the equilibrium in the exothermic direction, so the forward reaction must be exothermic.

The rising curves with pressure fit 2 mol of gas forming 1 mol, but that is a shift in position only: the equilibrium constant depends on temperature alone. For an exothermic forward reaction, K increases when the temperature is lowered.

optionAnalysis.text: Lower temperature gives more Z at equilibrium, so for this exothermic reaction K increases, not decreases.
Lowering the temperature always decreases the rate, because fewer collisions have energy at least equal to the activation energy. The graph shows equilibrium yields, not rates.
Pressure changes shift the position of equilibrium (more Z, fewer gas moles) but do not change the value of the equilibrium constant, which depends only on temperature.
Correct. The yield of Z rises as temperature falls, so the forward reaction releases heat.

reasoningChain: Read the graph at one pressure: % of Z increases as temperature decreases.
Le Chatelier: lowering temperature favours the exothermic direction, so forward is exothermic (D).
K depends only on temperature, so C is wrong; for an exothermic reaction K rises when T falls, so A is wrong.
Rate always falls at lower temperature, so B is wrong.

inferredMistakes.text: Mixing up equilibrium yield with rate and choosing B because lower temperatures give more Z.
Thinking that increasing pressure increases K because it increases the yield of Z.
